case_title: CHOTKAU v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was based on circumstantial evidence. On 8 March 2012, the accused took a minor girl under the pretense of showing dance and song performances during the Holi Festival. When the girl did not return home, a search was conducted, and her dead body was found in a sugarcane field. A villager claimed to have seen the accused leaving the field shortly after. The accused was charged with raping and murdering the girl. The prosecution relied on the testimonies of three witnesses who described the accused's actions and the location of the body. The accused denied the charges, claiming he was falsely implicated. The trial court and high court convicted the accused based on the circumstantial evidence and the last seen theory, but the Supreme Court found contradictions in the testimonies and the delay in transmitting the FIR to be fatal to the prosecution's case.
